title: Several tasks at once
sub: One by one, WhenAll and WhenAny
cards/0/body:
You can await three independent requests one by one: await, await, await. The times add up.

Or you can start all three at once and wait for them together with Task.WhenAll. Then it takes as long as the slowest one.
cards/1/task: Three requests: 300, 500 and 200 ms. Get the total time down to 500 ms or less.
cards/2/q: How long does the sequential version take?
cards/2/explain: 300 + 500 + 200. Each request starts after the previous one ends.
cards/3/task: Go back to "one by one" and make the first request fail. What happened to the others?
cards/4/q: With sequential awaits, why did B and C never even start after A failed?
cards/4/options/0: await A threw, and execution never reached the lines with B and C
cards/4/explain: An exception stops the method at the very first await.
cards/5/body:
Task.WhenAny returns the first task to finish. Handy for "whoever answers fastest" and for timeouts.

WhenAny itself doesn't throw: check the winner or await it.
cards/6/q: You need data from the fastest of three mirrors. What do you use?
cards/6/explain: Cancel the other tasks with a token so they don't waste resources.
cards/7/q: Why do the requests still run one by one?
cards/7/explain: The await inside the loop waits for each request before starting the next. Add the tasks themselves to the list, without await.
cards/8/q: Start all the requests at once
cards/8/explain: WhenAll returns an array of results in the same order.
